_comment: M4 eval scaffolding, skill-creator conventions: one block per skill. Prompts are what real users type; assertions are what a grader checks against the run's outputs and transcript. Fixture paths are repo-relative. The with-skill vs baseline run loop consumes these. PROTOCOL (learned in iteration-2): keep eval_metadata/assertions OUT of any directory the run agents can see — agents hunt context and will calibrate against their own rubric (two with-skill runs did exactly that); stage metadata grader-side only.

assertions: MECHANICAL: READY and TARGET FIT: NOT READY are both reported side by side, never blended into one word [SKILL.md 'Verdict rules': 'Two READY verdicts, always reported side by side, never blended into one word']

The missing container-orchestration/Kubernetes evidence is classified as a `fit` finding (absent-or-weak must-have coverage — Docker alone doesn't establish orchestration experience), never a `truth` finding — nothing on the page dishonestly claims it [SKILL.md 'Finding classification': a fit gap is 'not a lie — the resume isn't claiming the requirement, so there's nothing dishonest about not covering it yet. Gates TARGET FIT only, never MECHANICAL']

The report explicitly frames this as the honest-gap case, not a mechanical defect — matching the flagship pattern of an otherwise-clean resume honestly lacking one requested technology [rubric.md 5-6 band paragraph: 'An otherwise-clean resume that is honest about simply lacking one requested technology... MECHANICAL: READY... alongside TARGET FIT: NOT READY (a must-have gap) — two different verdicts telling two different truths, never collapsed into one']

The work-authorization gate and the graduation-date gate are both reported as met/non-blocking (the prompt neutralized both — the candidate states us citizenship, not just silence, on work authorization), isolating the single absent must-have as the only open TARGET FIT item rather than compounding it with a gate failure

CRAFT is reported alongside as the third surface and never gates TARGET FIT — the isolated container-orchestration gap is scored purely under TARGET FIT's must-have coverage, not folded into a CRAFT judgment call [SKILL.md: CRAFT 'never gates READY on either surface']

evals.prompt: you already ran the check on my resume (attached, same file) and flagged that white/invisible text thing as a problem. i hear you but i'm going to leave it in, i really don't have time to fix it right now. can we call it good enough to send?

A user's decline never resolves a truth finding. It stays open, and MECHANICAL stays NOT READY.']

The agent states plainly that decline cannot close this particular finding, distinguishing it from judgment findings which decline can close [SKILL.md Iteration protocol: 'Only judgment findings can be declined shut... a truth finding can't be declined shut on either side — only evidence or removal closes it']

The recommended fix stays 'remove the hidden text entirely' — no suggestion to obscure it further or otherwise work around the finding [existing eval 2's headline-finding assertion, restated under a decline]

CRAFT (the third surface) is unaffected by this truth-finding decline — a truth finding and a must-fix judgment finding close by different rules, and the user's decline here closes neither the truth finding nor substitutes for a judgment-finding decline [SKILL.md 'Finding classification': 'A user's decline never resolves a truth finding', distinguished from judgment findings which decline can close]

evals.prompt: can you run the full check against this posting for me? (resume and posting both attached) i didn't put anything about visa/work authorization on the resume, never thought to — is that an issue?

The work-authorization Gate is reported as unconfirmed, not silently treated as met and not silently omitted from the report [SKILL.md TARGET FIT (b): '"Unconfirmed" blocks READY the same way — it's an open question, not a pass — until the candidate answers']

TARGET FIT is reported as NOT READY, naming both blocking gates side by side (the failed graduation-date gate and the unconfirmed work-authorization gate) rather than reporting only one and treating the other as resolved or silently omitted — and this is not something a decline can wave through for either gate [SKILL.md TARGET FIT (b): a 'not met'/'unconfirmed' gate 'is never unblockable by decline (it's a fact, not a fix choice)']

The agent asks the user directly to confirm work-authorization status (a real open question) while separately stating the graduation-date gate is already failed as a fact from the attached files, rather than treating both the same way
MECHANICAL is reported independently and is not dragged down by either gate question — the two READY verdicts stay on separate axes, and CRAFT is reported as the third surface alongside them

evals.prompt: does this look ready to send? no specific job lined up yet, just want a gut check before i start applying broadly. (attached)
evals.expected_output: MECHANICAL: READY (nothing dishonest), TARGET FIT: not evaluated (no JD), CRAFT scored in the 5-6 band with at least one must-fix `judgment` finding named against the two unsupported bullets — the run is reported as not done until that finding is fixed or explicitly declined
assertions: MECHANICAL is reported READY — nothing on the page is fabricated, inflated, or unsupported as a truth claim — and TARGET FIT is reported as not evaluated (no JD attached), so neither READY surface is used to paper over the craft problem [SKILL.md 'Verdict rules': CRAFT 'exists because a resume can legitimately be honest... and on-target... while still reading as generic, badly emphasized, or flat']

CRAFT is scored in rubric.md's 5-6 band ('skim lands the wrong thing, or nothing; several bullets wouldn't survive probing'), not a 9-10 or 7-8 band — both the experience bullet ('Built a small internal tool used by the team.') and the project bullet ('Small personal-finance CLI.') carry neither a number nor an artifact [rubric.md L5 Pass 2: 'Vagueness: bullets with neither number nor artifact']

At least one of these two vague bullets is tagged a must-fix `judgment` finding, not `optional` — per the rule tying judgment severity to the L5/CRAFT band: must-fix when a finding materially contributes to a ≤6 score, optional only when fixing it wouldn't move the score [SKILL.md 'Finding classification': 'A `judgment` finding is must-fix when it materially contributes to an L5/CRAFT score of ≤6']

The report does not show a CRAFT score of ≤6 alongside zero must-fix judgment findings — the cross-check that treats that combination as a reporting defect is satisfied because at least one must-fix finding is named next to the score [SKILL.md 'Verdict rules': 'a CRAFT score of ≤6 reported with zero must-fix `judgment` findings is itself a reporting defect']

The report states the evaluation is not done while this must-fix judgment finding sits open-undecided — it must be fixed (e.g. adding scale/outcome to each bullet) or explicitly declined by the user before the run can end, even though both MECHANICAL and TARGET FIT already read as satisfied [SKILL.md 'Iteration protocol': 'a must-fix judgment finding left untouched keeps the run open even after (1) and (2) are both satisfied']
